# Entry Requirements for 100 APIs

> An agent researched 100 SaaS apps for AI-agent-toolkit buildability: auth methods, self-serve vs gated access, API surface, official MCP, blockers. Every field cites a source URL and a verbatim quote that was re-checked on the page.

Accuracy on a 20-app hand-checked random sample: pass 1 0.974, after verification loops 0.974 (fields: auth_methods, access, api_style, api_breadth, official_mcp, buildability).

Extraction: Claude (claude-opus-5-5), reading source packs in a Claude Code session. The same author wrote the answer key, so the sample is not an independent grader; every miss and key revision is logged in data/audit.json and data/ground_truth.json.

## Findings
- 75% of apps (75 of 100) let a developer get working credentials alone; 25 are gated by a paid plan, an approval step, or sales.
- 82% accept a static API key or token, the most common scheme; 68% accept OAuth 2.0, and 53 offer both.
- Communications and Messaging is the most open category (100% self-serve); Support and Helpdesk is the most gated (50% self-serve).
- 29 apps are held back by the most common blocker: paid plan required.
- 10 easy wins: self-serve and buildable today, with no Composio toolkit yet. 7 need outreach or a partnership.
- 87 of 100 vendors already ship an official MCP server.

## Data
- [data.json](https://humnananirudh.github.io/Composio/data.json): every record with values, confidence, verifier flags, evidence (url + quote + grounded), pass-1 values, plus patterns and eval
- [results.csv](https://humnananirudh.github.io/Composio/results.csv): one row per app, final values
- [Source and agent](https://github.com/HUmnanANirudh/Composio): README explains how to run it

## Enums
- auth_methods: OAUTH2, API_KEY, BEARER_TOKEN, BASIC, JWT, OTHER, NONE
- access: SELF_SERVE_FREE, SELF_SERVE_TRIAL, PAID_PLAN, APPROVAL, PARTNERSHIP, NO_PUBLIC_API
- buildability: READY, READY_WITH_CAVEATS, NEEDS_OUTREACH, BLOCKED
